blocks.text: The Sikhs protest that the Guru has chosen humble, unarmed people rather than royal warriors, but Guru Gobind Singh recognizes in that very hesitation the old psychology he now has to transform. (27–29)

He resolves to change both inner disposition and outer form: the old soft habits must give way to a martial bearing, new names, and khande-di-pahul so that the community can learn courage, sovereignty, and visible resolve. (30–34)
The goal is not merely military efficiency but a self-respecting Khalsa that bows to no earthly throne, carrying divine autonomy in its very appearance and conduct. (35)
